verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 22.88
verses.english: Linked Discourses 22.88

verses.pali: 9. Theravagga
verses.english: 9. Senior Mendicants

verses.pali: Assajisutta
verses.english: With Assaji

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā assaji kassapakārāme viharati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
verses.english: Now at that time Venerable Assaji was staying in a monastery built by a Kassapa, and he was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā assaji upaṭṭhāke āmantesi:
verses.english: Then he addressed his carers:

verses.pali: “etha tumhe, āvuso, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamatha; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatha:
verses.english: “Please, reverends, go to the Buddha, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:

verses.pali: ‘assaji, bhante, bhikkhu ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
verses.english: ‘Sir, the mendicant Assaji is sick, suffering, gravely ill.

verses.pali: So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti.
verses.english: He bows with his head to your feet.’

verses.pali: Evañca vadetha:
verses.english: And then say:

verses.pali: ‘sādhu kira, bhante, bhagavā yena assaji bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.
verses.english: ‘Sir, please go to the mendicant Assaji out of sympathy.’”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato assajissa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: “Yes, reverend,” those monks replied. They did as he asked.

verses.pali: “assaji, bhante, bhikkhu ābādhiko …pe…
sādhu kira, bhante, bhagavā yena assaji bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.
verses.english: The Buddha consented with silence.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā assaji tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to Venerable Assaji.

verses.pali: Addasā kho āyasmā assaji bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
verses.english: Venerable Assaji saw the Buddha coming off in the distance,

verses.pali: Disvāna mañcake samadhosi.
verses.english: and stirred in his cot.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ assajiṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: But the Buddha said to him,

verses.pali: “alaṁ, assaji, mā tvaṁ mañcake samadhosi.
verses.english: “It’s all right, Assaji, don’t get up.

verses.pali: Santimāni āsanāni paññattāni, tatthāhaṁ nisīdissāmī”ti.
verses.english: There are some seats spread out, I will sit there.”

verses.pali: Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ assajiṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: He sat on the seat spread out and said,

verses.pali: “kacci te, assaji, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ …pe… paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no abhikkamo”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you’re keeping well, Assaji; I hope you’re all right. And I hope the pain is fading, not growing, that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

verses.pali: “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ …pe… abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no paṭikkamo”ti.
verses.english: “Sir, I’m not all right, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading, its growing is evident, not its fading.”

verses.pali: “Kacci te, assaji, na kiñci kukkuccaṁ na koci vippaṭisāro”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you don’t have any remorse or regret?”

verses.pali: “Taggha me, bhante, anappakaṁ kukkuccaṁ anappako vippaṭisāro”ti.
verses.english: “Indeed, sir, I have no little remorse and regret.”

verses.pali: “Kacci pana taṁ, assaji, attā sīlato na upavadatī”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you have no reason to blame yourself when it comes to ethical conduct?”

verses.pali: “Na kho maṁ, bhante, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti.
verses.english: “No sir, I have no reason to blame myself when it comes to ethical conduct.”

verses.pali: “No ce kira taṁ, assaji, attā sīlato upavadati, atha kiñca te kukkuccaṁ ko ca vippaṭisāro”ti?
verses.english: “In that case, Assaji, why do you have remorse and regret?”

verses.pali: “Pubbe khvāhaṁ, bhante, gelaññe passambhetvā passambhetvā kāyasaṅkhāre viharāmi, sohaṁ samādhiṁ nappaṭilabhāmi.
verses.english: “Sir, before my time of illness I meditated having completely stilled the physical process. But now I can’t get immersion.

verses.pali: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, taṁ samādhiṁ appaṭilabhato evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: Since I can’t get immersion, I think:

verses.pali: ‘no cassāhaṁ parihāyāmī’”ti.
verses.english: ‘May I not decline!’”

verses.pali: “Ye te, assaji, samaṇabrāhmaṇā samādhisārakā samādhisāmaññā tesaṁ taṁ samādhiṁ appaṭilabhataṁ evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: “There are, Assaji, ascetics and brahmins for whom samādhi is the essence, equating immersion with the ascetic life. They think:

verses.pali: ‘no cassu mayaṁ parihāyāmā’ti.
verses.english: ‘May we not decline!’

verses.pali: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, assaji,
verses.english: What do you think, Assaji?

verses.pali: rūpaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: Is form permanent or impermanent?”

verses.pali: “Aniccaṁ, bhante” …pe…
verses.english: “Impermanent, sir.” …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ …pe…
verses.english: “Is consciousness permanent or impermanent?” …

verses.pali: “tasmātiha …pe…
verses.english: “So you should truly see …

verses.pali: evaṁ passaṁ …pe…
verses.english: Seeing this …

verses.pali: nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānātīti.
verses.english: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’

verses.pali: So sukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, sā ‘aniccā’ti pajānāti. ‘Anajjhositā’ti pajānāti. ‘Anabhinanditā’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: If they feel a pleasant feeling, they understand that it’s impermanent, that they’re not attached to it, and that they don’t relish it.

verses.pali: Dukkhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, sā ‘aniccā’ti pajānāti. ‘Anajjhositā’ti pajānāti. ‘Anabhinanditā’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: If they feel a painful feeling, they understand that it’s impermanent, that they’re not attached to it, and that they don’t relish it.

verses.pali: Adukkhamasukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, sā ‘aniccā’ti pajānāti …pe… ‘anabhinanditā’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: If they feel a neutral feeling, they understand that it’s impermanent, that they’re not attached to it, and that they don’t relish it.

verses.pali: So sukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, visaṁyutto naṁ vedayati;
verses.english: If they feel a pleasant feeling, they feel it detached.

verses.pali: dukkhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, visaṁyutto naṁ vedayati;
verses.english: If they feel a painful feeling, they feel it detached.

verses.pali: adukkhamasukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, visaṁyutto naṁ vedayati.
verses.english: If they feel a neutral feeling, they feel it detached.

verses.pali: So kāyapariyantikañce vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti. Jīvitapariyantikañce vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: Feeling the end of the body draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of the body draw close.’ Feeling the end of life draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of life draw close.’

verses.pali: ‘Kāyassa bhedā uddhaṁ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītībhavissantī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life is over, everything that’s felt, being no longer relished, will become cool right here.’

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, assaji, telañca paṭicca, vaṭṭiñca paṭicca, telappadīpo jhāyeyya;
verses.english: Suppose an oil lamp depended on oil and a wick to burn.

verses.pali: tasseva telassa ca vaṭṭiyā ca pariyādānā anāhāro nibbāyeyya.
verses.english: As the oil and the wick are used up, it would be extinguished due to not being fed.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, assaji, bhikkhu kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti. Jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayamāno ‘jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vedayāmī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: In the same way, feeling the end of the body draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of the body draw close.’ Feeling the end of life draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of life draw close.’

verses.pali: ‘Kāyassa bhedā uddhaṁ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītībhavissantī’ti pajānātī”ti.
verses.english: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life is over, everything that’s felt, being no longer relished, will become cool right here.’”

verses.pali: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
